display: Board-certified music therapist from Vancouver, on a sabbatical year in Dali, learning Mandarin and playing guitar in the old town on weekends.

signals.text: I'm looking for a clinic, care home or hospital in Dali or Kunming where a music therapist can sit in on or run sessions under a supervisor.
I need roughly a hundred documented, supervised clinical contact hours before next summer to keep my certification on track.
Most places I've approached say they can't take a foreign trainee, or want Mandarin fluency I don't have yet.
I'm trying to rest without apologising for it, while also not coming back to work deskilled. Holding both is tiring.
I miss the clinical work more than I expected after nine months away.
I'm learning Mandarin and will start on hospital vocabulary this week. I'd like practice with real conversations, not just lessons.
I'm curious about Bai folk music and want to hear and understand more of it. Someone has a wall of old Bai cassette tapes at the market.
I'd like to find older local people or elder-care settings where shared songs could be welcome.
My family is going through a house move back in Canada, and I'm helping from far away.
I'm still sorting out visa and paperwork logistics in Dali and could use local practical know-how.
Busking by the old-town bridge on Saturdays only covers strings and lunch, and I'd like to play in more places.
I'm trying to work out what kind of music therapy work I want to come back to.

offers.text: Board-certified music therapist (MT-BC) with six years of clinical work in hospice and dementia care.
Designing and leading group sessions for older adults, including familiar-song groups, rhythm work, reminiscence and life review.
Training or briefing for carers and volunteers on using familiar music with people with dementia or at end of life.
Clinical documentation habits: SOAP notes, goal tracking, and baseline and follow-up observations. I can help set up simple outcome tracking.
A travel guitar, a frame drum, a small set of tuned percussion and a portable speaker, all ready for sessions or small events.
English native speaker who can do conversation practice, and can help with English-language materials for a clinic or school.
Live acoustic guitar and voice for community events, cafés or gatherings in Dali, as a volunteer or for tips.
Knowledge of how music therapy certification, continuing education and supervision work in North America.
Time for volunteer sessions, since I'm on sabbatical and flexible during weekdays.

catchers.hypo: I run a small elder-care home near Dali and some of our residents with memory loss are agitated in the afternoons. Do you know anyone who could run a music session?
catchers.can: Design and lead a regular group session with the home's carers, document goals and responses, and show staff simple routines they can keep using.
catchers.confirm: Could a licensed or experienced professional supervise or countersign documented session notes?

catchers.hypo: I'm a doctor or therapist in Kunming or Dali with a patient group that could benefit from music. I'd like a certified music therapist to observe or co-lead, and I can formally supervise.
catchers.can: Do supervised, documented clinical contact hours. This is exactly the setup that would count toward my certification.
catchers.confirm: Can you or a colleague sign off as an approved supervisor, with written session records, for at least twenty hours a month?

catchers.hypo: I teach Mandarin or run a language exchange in Dali. Would a foreign music therapist like to trade English or music sessions for hospital-vocabulary practice?
catchers.can: Offer English conversation or a music session in exchange for focused practice on medical and care vocabulary.
catchers.confirm: Can the practice focus on hospital and care-setting vocabulary and not general conversation?

catchers.hypo: My grandmother in the old town has dementia. She used to sing Bai songs, and nobody in the family knows what to do with her afternoons.
catchers.can: Suggest simple ways to use familiar songs and rhythm at home, and tell the family what to look for. Where the family is local, I could visit informally.
catchers.confirm: Do you have access to recordings or can you name a few songs she used to sing or hum?

catchers.hypo: I collect old Bai folk cassettes and would like someone to help me work out which songs would suit a listening group for elders.
catchers.can: Listen with them and help judge which tracks might work for a group, with the local collector or an elder on hand to explain them.
catchers.confirm: Can a Bai speaker or a person who knows the songs be present to explain what they mean?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse or care worker, tired and a bit burnt out from long-term care. Could someone who has done it talk with me?
catchers.can: Talk honestly about sustaining caring work, and share what I've found helps in hospice and dementia settings.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a peer conversation and not for formal counselling or a clinical referral?

catchers.hypo: My mother is also downsizing and sorting a lifetime of boxes. Is there anyone who could help me think about what to keep and how to talk about it?
catchers.can: Through my mother's recent move in Burnaby, offer a few real, practical ideas from someone who just lived the conversation. I could connect them with her if both are willing.
catchers.confirm: Is the move happening in the Vancouver area, and is the family open to a short chat with someone who has just gone through it?

catchers.hypo: I'm Ms. Yang's friend and run a retired teachers' group in Dali. We would like an activity with songs and a guest from abroad.
catchers.can: Run a singalong or reminiscence session for the group, with help from my Mandarin tutor and her contacts as interpreters.
catchers.confirm: Can someone in the group translate between Mandarin and English during the session?

catchers.hypo: I'm a music therapist or student abroad hoping to practise in a place with few resources. How did you find your placement?
catchers.can: Share what I've tried so far in Yunnan, which approaches failed and which are worth a try, and compare notes. I'd welcome hearing what has worked for others.
catchers.confirm: Are you also looking for in-person, documented hours for a board-certified credential?

forbids.text: I can't take paid work in China on my current visa, so any arrangement has to be unpaid, volunteer or expenses only.
Clinical hours only count with an approved supervisor and documentation, so I won't offer informal sessions as clinical treatment.
I won't discuss or share details of former clients or patients.
My Mandarin is limited and I have no Bai, so I need an interpreter for anything that depends on precise language.
I'm only in Dali until about next summer, so I can't commit to anything that runs longer.

projects.name: Supervised music therapy hours in Yunnan
projects.text: I'm looking for a setting in Dali or Kunming where I can run or co-run music sessions for older adults, with a supervisor who can sign off documented hours.

policy.t1: Clinical background, session design, equipment and credential rules, once there is a real chance of a placement, session or conversation.
policy.t2: The credential hours shortfall, family changes and what I'm unsure about regarding my next steps, once I know who the other person is and the fit looks strong.
policy.never: Names and details of former clients, and any session content from them.
